note: Order every 2 days, 2-day demand ×1.1 (≈5% over the mean multiplier). Risk: the stock buffer may be too thin for product 1, whose shortage is expensive.
Order every 2 days, product 1 ×1.25 and product 0 ×1.15, smaller last orders. Risk: holding cost and getting close to the 220 limit around day 24.
Order every 3 days ×1.2, saving on the 59 fixed fee per order day. Risk: more holding cost and possible overflow at peak arrivals.
Daily orders of one day's demand ×1.2 (minimal stock). Risk: about 1650 in fixed order fees eats more than the holding cost saved.
Lean version: every 2 days, exactly the forecast. Risk: the mean multiplier is 1.046, so there will be regular product 1 shortages with penalties.
Aggressive stock: every 2 days, ×1.4 / ×1.3. Risk: excess builds up, raising holding cost, spoilage and overflow at the 220 limit.
Order every 3 days with a small buffer (×1.08). Risk: shortages at the end of each 3-day cycle, given the high demand variance.
Hybrid: product 1 every 2 days ×1.2, product 0 in 4-day batches on the same days (no extra fixed fee). Risk: higher product 0 holding cost and tight space when large batches arrive.
